Rowan/hellaswag.name: HellaSwag
Rowan/hellaswag.provider: Rowan Zellers / University of Washington & Allen Institute for AI
Rowan/hellaswag.description: A commonsense natural language inference benchmark of multiple-choice sentence-completion problems designed to be trivial for humans but hard for machines (ACL 2019).
Rowan/hellaswag.size: 10,042 validation examples (39,905 train, 10,003 test with hidden labels)

reference.title: HellaSwag: Can a Machine Really Finish Your Sentence?

allenai/winogrande.name: Winogrande
allenai/winogrande.description: A large-scale collection of fill-in-the-blank commonsense reasoning problems adjusted from the Winograd Schema Challenge to reduce annotation artifacts and dataset-specific bias.
allenai/winogrande.size: 1,267 validation examples (winogrande_xl: 40,398 train, 1,767 test with hidden labels)

lukaemon/bbh.name: BIG-Bench Hard
lukaemon/bbh.provider: Suzgun et al. (Stanford University / Google Research authors)
lukaemon/bbh.description: A curated suite of 23 challenging tasks from BIG-Bench where prior language models did not outperform average human raters, used to study chain-of-thought prompting.
lukaemon/bbh.size: 27 task configs, 250 test examples each for most tasks (6,511 examples total)

reference.title: Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them

slug:agieval-english.name: AGIEval (English subset)
slug:agieval-english.provider: Ruixiang Cui et al. (Microsoft Research / Westlake University)
slug:agieval-english.description: The English-language subtasks (e.g. AQuA-RAT, LogiQA-EN, LSAT-AR/LR/RC, SAT-EN, SAT-Math) of AGIEval, a human-centric benchmark built from real-world standardized admission and qualification exams.
slug:agieval-english.size: 9 English-language exam subtasks (task sizes range from ~230 to ~1,000 examples each)

slug:boolq.name: BoolQ
slug:boolq.description: A question-answering dataset of naturally occurring yes/no questions paired with a supporting passage, used to study surprisingly hard inference over unconstrained real-world questions.

reference.title: BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions

slug:commonsenseqa.name: CommonsenseQA
slug:commonsenseqa.provider: Tel Aviv University / Allen Institute for AI
slug:commonsenseqa.description: A multiple-choice commonsense question answering dataset built from ConceptNet, where each question has one correct answer and four distractors requiring commonsense knowledge to resolve.
slug:commonsenseqa.size: 1,221 validation examples (9,741 train, 1,140 test with hidden labels)

reference.title: CommonsenseQA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge
